batch_notes: Nine of ten targets are uv crates (plus url and unicode-segmentation) whose main properties are differential tests against PyPA packaging or pip run as a persistent Python child, so external-oracle dominates. Recurring shapes the rubric handles unevenly: (1) split-then-concatenate-is-identity (unicode-segmentation) sits between roundtrip and spec-postcondition; classified spec-postcondition (partition well-formedness) because the inverse is std concatenation, not a library operation. (2) 'wrapper op equals op on the underlying type' (uom atan2 vs add_homomorphism) reads as external-oracle or algebraic-law depending on the doc's framing; followed the doc lead each time. (3) The uv forks carry many properties that were pins in the origin crate (pep440_rs, pep508_rs) but hold here because the fork fixed the bug ('Holds in uv-... (X was fixed in the fork)'): they are narrowed like pins yet find no bug, so they were not tagged pin; they inflate the count of narrow properties without a bug. (4) Nearly every uv bug is recorded with its own narrowed generative property named after the intended behaviour (e.g. build_tag_digits_are_unbounded) rather than an example pin, so the bug records already carry property ids and only two attributions were needed; these were tagged pin. (5) uv-pep440's properties have no doc comments (README carries prose descriptions instead), and uv-pypi-types lenient_parsing_is_transparent_on_valid_input draws only from fixed pools (REQUIREMENTS, SPECIFIER_SETS), so it is closer to a parameterised example test than a generative property. (6) url hegel_arbitrary_setter_values_keep_url_reparseable is a short random op sequence checked only at the end against invariants, tagged stateful but not classified stateful-model since there is no model and no per-step check.
